reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only generally states that MLIPs are accurate for melting temperature predictions and that ab initio simulations are resource-consuming, but it provides no specific support for the key premises about improved phase-space overlap, reduced integration path mismatch, or the inadequacy of EAM references for liquid configurations. The evidence does not address thermodynamic integration or compare MLIPs to EAM potentials.
premises: MLIPs can be trained on diverse ab initio configurations of both solid and liquid states at high temperatures.
MLIPs better represent many-body and short-range correlation effects than EAM potentials.
Improved phase-space overlap from MLIPs minimizes thermodynamic integration path mismatch.
EAM references in TOR-TILD poorly represent the diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid state.
MLIPs are applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
